title: How would you estimate how many full-time wedding photographers the UK needs?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many full-time wedding photographers does the UK need?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A short, two-step estimate that rewards thinking about the season: most weddings happen on summer weekends. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many full-time wedding photographers does the UK need?

The approach

Weddings per year ÷ weddings one photographer can shoot per year.

Tip: Name the assumption that matters most, so the interviewer knows where the estimate is most sensitive.

Step by step

  1. Weddings in the UK per year: 250k
  2. ÷ 25 weddings one photographer can do per year (mostly summer weekends)

That gives about 10k photographers.

Does it make sense?

Plenty of photographers also work part time, so the real number of people doing some weddings will be higher.

Weddings may require more than one photographer

The original division gives 10,000 full-time equivalents at 25 weddings per photographer per year. It assumes one photographer per wedding. Suppose 30% of couples also hire a second shooter. That increases photographer assignments from 250,000 to 325,000, raising the required full-time-equivalent supply to 13,000 on the same workload assumption.

Seasonality is the next constraint. A photographer cannot spread every wedding evenly across 52 weekends. Popular summer Saturdays may be full while midweek capacity goes unused. Some professionals therefore mix wedding work with portraits, events and commercial assignments.

Ask whether the interviewer wants the number of working photographers, their full-time-equivalent capacity or annual customer spending. For spending, a fee per booked wedding would be needed; dividing weddings by assignments alone cannot answer it.
